decisions.topic: Composite fonts are a CMap code-to-CID mapping plus an independent CID-to-glyph mapping
decisions.check: Current CodeMapping::Composite preserves both maps separately. CMap code length/value and the CID-to-glyph route are visible in loading/codes.rs, composite.rs, and loading/glyphs.rs. Existing tests distinguish variable-width codes, a nonidentity predefined CMap, W indexed by CID, and mapped GIDs.
decisions.limit: Some corpus checks skip when optional corpus checkout is absent; deterministic map stream fixture draft addresses one specific gap.

decisions.topic: Carry and resolve required predefined CMap data
decisions.check: §9.7.5.2 says a processor shall support Adobe-CNS1-7, Adobe-GB1-5, Adobe-Japan1-7, Adobe-KR-9. Current data/cmaps contains compiled data and predefined tests; named mapping tests use Adobe 90ms-RKSJ-H. No contrary source evidence found.
decisions.status: Retain for this shard; all names/data and licensing were not recounted.

decisions.topic: Read an Encoding CMap bfrange array destination as the stated CID mapping although §9.7.5.4 c constrains producers
decisions.check: The source distinction is sound: §9.7.5.4 c is a producer constraint, while §9.7.6.2 lists bfchar and corresponding ranges in the reader's lookup. Current parser's stride/resynchronization and tests were inspected. This is an explicit malformed-input recovery choice, not a claim of required conforming-file behavior.

decisions.topic: Hollow embedded Type2 font with a remapping stream does not collapse metrics-derived text geometry
decisions.check: Source clauses separate glyph outline selection from text geometry; tests in test-scenes/ocr_text_layer use a hollow loca and CIDToGIDMap remapping, with nonempty expected CID width statements, and assert extracted text, shape counts and selection bands. The implementation does not infer selection geometry from outlines.
decisions.status: Retain for the tested CSDK fixture; fixture maker's map-generation helpers are not an independent numeric oracle.

decisions.topic: Type1 dictionary over OpenType CFF uses §9.6.5.2 glyph-name selection rather than TrueType cmap route
decisions.check: Table 124/§9.9.1 selection bullets and changed opening.rs helper agree. `opentype_selection_audit.rs` uses exact xref and distinct GID expectations; CFF's post v3 omits names and its cmap offers conflicting glyphs, making route selection observable. The same CFF bare Type1C and glyf controls pass at the assertion level.
decisions.status: Retain for the specific selection premise; not full OpenType conformance.

decisions.topic: Draw from a substitute face for a present but unreadable embedded font program
decisions.check: §9.5 and §9.8.1 permit substitute selection for an unavailable program but do not require this particular recovery. Current helper retains the originating refusal and excludes no-code-reaches-glyph. This is a product policy decision rather than an OpenType/CID conformance duty.
decisions.status: No reconsideration from this bounded CID/OpenType pass.
decisions.limit: The new unreadable-program substitution tests and actual host report contract were not exhaustively reviewed here.

draft.basis: Table 115 bytes 2*c and 2*c+1 with high-order byte first; §9.7.6.3 says if Type2 CIDToGIDMap stream has no GID for a code, substitute the glyph for CID 0.
draft.assertions: CID 5 has GID 37 from bytes 10-11 (positive mapped control); CID 6 is beyond the 12-byte map and falls back through CID 0 to GID 36. The PDF uses exact offsets, asserts !was_recovered(), real nonempty outlines and public interpretation glyph count.
draft.execution: Draft only; parent has not promoted or run it.
